title: Annotatio II §.VII: Lateran names Consubstantiation as already exploded — true accidents and true substance remain
pass_a_gloss: There were, it says, who would say that just as after Consecration the true accidents of bread remain, so also the true substance of bread: because just as a subject cannot subsist without Accidents, so Accidents cannot subsist without a subject.
pass_b_english: Some said: after consecration, as true bread-accidents remain, so true bread-substance remains.
For a subject cannot stand without accidents, nor accidents without a subject.
source_text: Fuerunt, inquit, qui dicerent, quòd sicut post Consecrationem, vera panis remanent accidentia sic & vera panis substantia: quia sicut subjectum non potest subsistere sine Accidentibus, sic Accidentia non possunt subsistere sine subjecto.
